notes: Four UVM documents (Code of Academic Integrity, About AI, WID teaching guide, Writing Centers guide); both coders gave the same stance for all four (restrict, permit, delegates, delegates). Matching was done by source passage. Disagreements: (1) policy type, mostly between neighbouring types: P01/P06 on the Code's default ban (P01 chosen; P06 is for a silent syllabus), P09/P55/P18 on rationale and syllabus-content sentences (P09 chosen), P36/P37/P77 on advice to link or state consequences (P77, P37), P15/P18 on the Cumming sample (P15 with a fit_note), P99/P35 on the 'numerous opportunities' item (P99), P57/P34 and P39/P82 on the WID instructor-practice advice (P57, P39), P24/P25/P92/P50/P72 in the Writing Centers guide (settled sentence by sentence). (2) modality: 'informs' versus 'may', 'should' or 'should-not' on descriptions of what AI tools can do or what is wise; resolved to the source verb: 'can help/could' stays informs, 'avoid' is should-not, 'reserve the right' is may. (3) phase: general versus before-course/course-start/during-work; resolved by whether the sentence is tied to a stage of a course. (4) one actor split (all versus student) on the 'integrity policy set up by the instructor' sentence. Units found by one coder: coder A split sentences more finely (WID sample statements, definitions on the About page, hearing procedure of the Code); coder B coded some single sentences as one unit where A coded two. Kept: all only-A and only-B units that state AI-related advice or rules (including all AI definitions and the sample-statement sentences) except the Code's general hearing procedure (5 units), the About page's bare 'Effective Date' line (coder B) and the Writing Centers 'Howe Library, Student Guide to AI' list entry (coder A). Where the two coders anchored the same sentence on different clauses I treated them as a match.
